claims.statement: The fixture typechecks clean on its own under tsc 7.0.2 with zero diagnostics; a contract-violating caller is the negative control.

Two minimalist competing method vocabularies were built and compared as executable probes (v1-verbs, v2-predicates) with a deterministic comparison harness; the review round found them TIED on three of four criteria, so neither is selected.

Arm C meets its prompt-derived acceptance checklist on all substantive criteria (35 pass). Two criteria — M1 'repo commit pinned AND still matches live HEAD' and M18 'HEAD unchanged and all run output is untracked' — now FAIL, and that is expected rather than a regression.
Blind-discovery exclusions (other arms, the legacy alignment map) are disclosed in the run note rather than silently relied upon.
The three-operation vocabulary exists/witnessed/enforced is a live contender but NOT frozen: n=1 fixture cannot adjudicate it, and WikiCore remains a working name, not an approved protocol.
Whether the recovered 17-family symbolic lexer is a better intake than the probes built here was not tested by this run.

publication.reason: Run note, acceptance checklist, evidence JSONs and executable probes.

extensions.expired_criteria: M1 and M18 assert REPOSITORY STATE (pinned commit still equals live HEAD; run output still untracked), not artifact quality. Both were true when the run executed and are now false only because the round has since been legitimately committed on labs/elephant-lab-operations. The check therefore has a design flaw worth recording generally: a self-verification that measures repository state will always go red once the work is committed, so it measures hygiene at a moment in time rather than the quality of the evidence. Arm C's own artifacts were NOT edited to make it pass — doing so would tamper with the evidence. This is recorded here, in a generated receipt, instead.
